title: Account Wiring Brief — 45m activation playbook + preflight
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact 45-minute playbook for accounts that are in the activation -> expansion window (30–90 days before renewal). The goal is to align exec stakeholders, validate technical wiring, capture blockers that could impact renewal, and leave with clear next steps and owners.

When to use (quick heuristic):
- Account shows strong product usage but has 2+ open integration tickets, or
- Renewal window < 90 days and onboarding is not fully complete, or
- Customer requested a short executive sync to confirm timelines.

Audience (recommended attendees):
- Customer: 1 exec sponsor, 1 technical lead (integration owner), 1 PM or product lead (optional)
- Redwood: Customer Success Manager (facilitator), Solutions Engineer (technical verification), Account Executive (renewal owner), Implementation PM (if applied)

Desired outcomes (what we want at EOM):
- Confirm production readiness checklist (yes/no) + owner for outstanding items
- Agreement on renewal posture and any commercial asks to surface to AE
- 1–3 prioritized action items with owners and due dates

45-minute run-of-show (timed agenda)
0:00–0:03 — Welcome & framing (CSM)
- Quick intros (name, role, one-sentence success metric).
- State meeting goals: "Validate wiring, identify roadblocks, agree next steps."

0:03–0:10 — Executive readout (customer exec)
- Customer to share 1–2 top business outcomes they need from Redwood in next 90 days.
- CSM notes any shift in priority or new stakeholders.

0:10–0:25 — Technical wiring check (Solutions Engineer + Tech lead)
- Confirm production endpoints, auth/KMS keys, VPC peering, routing, and deployment cadence.
- Live checklist (call out any missing items):
  - Integration test results? (pass/fail)
  - Data ingress/egress confirmed? (any PII concerns?)
  - Latency/throughput expectations vs. observed?
- If any infra blocker: declare "severity" and mitigation owner.

0:25–0:35 — Risk & timeline alignment (CSM + AE)
- Renewal posture quick poll (green/amber/red) + reason.
- Map outstanding technical items to timeline impact (e.g., blocks GA, may delay renewal).
- AE to surface any commercial levers if renewal at risk.

0:35–0:42 — Decisions and commitments
- Capture up to 3 action items with owner and firm due date.
- Confirm follow-up cadence (quick standup vs. 30-day checkpoint).

0:42–0:45 — Close and quick retro (CSM)
- "One thing we need from you" ask for the customer (e.g., test data, security contact).
- Quick confirmation of next meeting and ownership.

Facilitation script (short lines for CSM):
- Opening line: "Thanks all — today we’ll run a tight 45 so we can leave with a clear plan and owners. If there are any deep technicals we’ll capture them and have Solutions follow up."
- If meeting drifts: "We’re running short — can we capture this as a follow-up action and continue with the top items?"
- If exec raises a new priority: "That sounds important — can we bracket that as a scope item and confirm whether it affects the existing timeline?"

Preflight checklist for CSM (complete before meeting):
- Confirm attendee list + roles (email confirmations).
- Pull latest integration test logs and latency dashboard snapshot. (attach to invite)
- Create a shared doc with live action tracker (link in calendar).
- Brief Solutions Engineer on expected ask areas.
- AE to confirm any commercial signals/discount runway.

Engineering readiness quick checklist for SE (what to verify live):
- API keys: valid, least-privilege, stored in customer KMS?
- Network: VPC peering / firewall rules tested from customer infra to Redwood endpoints.
- Model variant pinned? (if customer uses a specific variant for compliance)
- Observability hooks installed (logs, tracing) with access granted to Redwood support.

Decision grid (one-page mental model):
- Green: No blockers; onboarding >80% complete; renewal likely — focus on expansion use-cases.
- Amber: 1–2 medium blockers (integration/observability) — negotiate timeline and assign resources.
- Red: Major blocker (security signoff, billing/legal hold) — escalate to AE and Solutions leadership.

Common escalation contacts (carry in calendar):
- Solutions Eng lead: Jonas Keller — for urgent infra escalations
- SRE on-call: use SRE rota link in shared doc
- AE: Eileen Wu — commercial commitments and renewal conversations

Email template for follow-up (post-meeting):
Subject: Recap + actions from 45m activation sync — [Account Name] — [date]

Hi [Customer Sponsor],
Thanks for the time today. Quick recap below:
- Outcome: [Green/Amber/Red] and reason
- Action items:
  1) Owner — action — due date
  2) Owner — action — due date
- Next meeting: [date/time] (or cadence)
If anything above looks off, please flag — otherwise we’ll proceed with these commitments.
Best,
Maya (CSM)

Notes to self / open questions (keep here):
- Do we want a separate "security town hall" if customer is amber due to SOC/ISO items? (pros/cons)
- Can we offer a short, 1-week SE immersion to unblock integration? Cost/approval?
- Template hookup: add a checkbox for "legal review required" in the preflight doc.

Appendix: quick prompts for the Technical Lead
- "What is the expected QPS and what load test have you run?"
- "Do you have an expiration policy for API keys and who rotates them?"
- "Any third-party proxies/load balancers between your infra and Redwood?"

Versioning / audit trail
- Keep this doc as the baseline for the action tracker; move final actions to CS tracker JIRA ticket (linked).

Quick file housekeeping (where to store artifacts):
- Meeting notes: attach to account Confluence page (CONFLUENCE-1234).
- Action tickets: create in JIRA with CS label and link back here.

End of doc.
